verses.1:1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
verses.1:2: Just as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Behold, I am sending My messenger before Your face, who shall prepare Your way;
verses.1:3: a voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight His paths,'"
verses.1:4: John came forth, baptizing in the wilderness and preaching a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
verses.1:5: And all the countryside of Judea and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
verses.1:6: Now John was arrayed in camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
verses.1:7: And he was preaching, saying, "One mightier than I comes after me, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loose;
verses.1:8: I baptized you with water, but He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
verses.1:9: And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and He was baptized in the Jordan by John.
verses.1:10: And immediately, coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit, like a dove, descending upon Him;
verses.1:11: and a voice came from the heavens: "You are My Son, the Beloved; in You I am well pleased."
verses.1:12: And immediately the Spirit drove Him forth into the wilderness.
verses.1:13: And He was in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by Satan; and He was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to Him.
verses.1:14: And after John had been delivered up, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of God,
verses.1:15: and saying, "The appointed time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent, and believe in the gospel."
verses.1:16: And as He passed along by the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.1:17: And Jesus said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men."
verses.1:18: And immediately, leaving the nets, they followed Him.
verses.1:19: And going forward a little, He saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets,
verses.1:20: and immediately He called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, they went away after Him.
verses.1:21: And they entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath He went into the synagogue and began teaching.
verses.1:22: And they were astounded at His teaching, for He was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
verses.1:23: And immediately there was a man in their synagogue with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
verses.1:24: saying, "What have we to do with You, Jesus the Nazarene? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!"
verses.1:25: And Jesus rebuked it, saying, "Be silent, and come out of him!"
verses.1:26: And having convulsed him and cried out with a loud voice, the unclean spirit came out of him.
verses.1:27: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, "What is this? A new teaching! With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him."
verses.1:28: And immediately the report about Him went out everywhere into the entire surrounding region of Galilee.
verses.1:29: And immediately, coming out of the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
verses.1:30: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying ill with a fever, and immediately they spoke to Him concerning her.
verses.1:31: And coming near, He raised her up, taking her by the hand; and the fever left her, and she ministered to them.
verses.1:32: Now when evening came, when the sun had set, they were bringing to Him all who were ill and those who were demon-possessed;
verses.1:33: and the entire city was assembled together at the door.
verses.1:34: And He healed many who were ill with various diseases, and He cast out many demons; and He did not permit the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
verses.1:35: And rising early in the morning, while it was still very dark, He went out and departed to a solitary place, and there He was praying.
verses.1:36: And Simon and those with him searched diligently for Him,
verses.1:37: and they found Him and said to Him, "Everyone is seeking You."
verses.1:38: And He said to them, "Let us go elsewhere into the neighboring towns, that I may preach there also; for to this end I came forth."
verses.1:39: And He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
verses.1:40: And a leper came to Him, pleading with Him and kneeling down, saying to Him, "If You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.1:41: And moved with compassion, He stretched forth His hand, touched him, and said to him, "I am willing; be cleansed."
verses.1:42: And immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
verses.1:43: And having sternly warned him, He immediately sent him away,
verses.1:44: and He said to him, "See that you tell no one anything; rather, go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
verses.1:45: But having gone out, he began to proclaim it widely and to spread abroad the report, so that He was no longer able to enter a city openly, but remained outside in desolate places; and they were coming to Him from every quarter.
verses.2:1: And when He entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that He was at home.
verses.2:2: And many gathered together, so that there was no longer room, not even near the door; and He was speaking the word to them.
verses.2:3: And they came to Him, bringing a paralytic carried by four men.
verses.2:4: And being unable to bring him to Him because of the multitude, they uncovered the roof where He was; and when they had dug through, they let down the pallet on which the paralytic lay.
verses.2:5: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, "Child, your sins are forgiven."
verses.2:6: Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning within their hearts,
verses.2:7: "Why does this Man speak like this? He blasphemes! Who can forgive sins except God alone?"
verses.2:8: And immediately Jesus, discerning in His spirit that they reasoned thus within themselves, said to them, "Why do you reason about these things in your hearts?
verses.2:9: Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Arise, take up your pallet, and walk'?
verses.2:10: Yet so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins"—He said to the paralytic—
verses.2:11: "I say to you, arise, take up your pallet, and go to your house."
verses.2:12: And he arose, and immediately picking up the pallet, he went out before them all, so that all were astonished and glorified God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this!"
verses.2:13: And He went out again beside the sea; and all the multitude was coming to Him, and He was teaching them.
verses.2:14: And as He passed by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And rising up, he followed Him.
verses.2:15: And it came to pass, as He reclined at table in his house, that many tax collectors and sinners also reclined with Jesus and His disciples; for there were many, and they were following Him.
verses.2:16: And when the scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, they said to His disciples, "Why does He eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.2:17: When Jesus heard it, He said to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.2:18: Now the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting. And they came and said to Him, "Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.2:19: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
verses.2:20: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
verses.2:21: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise, the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear is made.
verses.2:22: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine is destroyed, and the wineskins as well. Rather, new wine belongs in fresh wineskins."
verses.2:23: Now it happened that He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to make their way, plucking the heads of grain.
verses.2:24: And the Pharisees said to Him, "Behold, why do they do on the Sabbath what is not lawful?"
verses.2:25: And He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and grew hungry, he and those who were with him?
verses.2:26: How he entered the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence, which is not lawful for any to eat except the priests, and also gave some to those who were with him?"
verses.2:27: And He said to them, "The Sabbath was made for the sake of man, and not man for the sake of the Sabbath.
verses.2:28: So then, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
verses.3:1: And He entered a synagogue again, and a man was there who had a withered hand.
verses.3:2: And they were watching Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
verses.3:3: And He said to the man who had the withered hand, "Stand up in the midst."
verses.3:4: And He said to them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" Yet they kept silent.
verses.3:5: And having looked around at them with wrath, deeply grieved at the hardness of their heart, He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
verses.3:6: And the Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against Him, how they might destroy Him.
verses.3:7: And Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea; and a great multitude from Galilee followed, and from Judea,
verses.3:8: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all the things that He was doing, came to Him.
verses.3:9: And He told His disciples that a small boat should be kept ready for Him because of the multitude, lest they crush Him;
verses.3:10: for He had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing upon Him in order to touch Him.
verses.3:11: And the unclean spirits, whenever they beheld Him, fell down before Him and cried out, saying, "You are the Son of God!"
verses.3:12: And He sternly charged them that they should not make Him known.
verses.3:13: And He went up on the mountain and summoned those whom He Himself desired, and they came to Him.
verses.3:14: And He appointed twelve, whom He also named apostles, that they might be with Him and that He might send them forth to preach,
verses.3:15: and to have authority to cast out the demons.
verses.3:16: Thus He appointed the twelve: and to Simon He gave the name Peter,
verses.3:17: and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James (and He gave them the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder),
verses.3:18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
verses.3:19: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed Him.
verses.3:20: Then He came home; and the multitude assembled again, so that they were not even able to eat bread.
verses.3:21: And when His own people heard of it, they went out to lay hold of Him, for they were saying, "He is out of His mind."
verses.3:22: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons."
verses.3:23: So He summoned them to Himself and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan cast out Satan?
verses.3:24: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom is not able to stand.
verses.3:25: And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
verses.3:26: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he is not able to stand, but has an end.
verses.3:27: Yet no one is able to enter the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
verses.3:28: Assuredly, I say to you, all things shall be forgiven the sons of men—the sins and whatever blasphemies they may utter;
verses.3:29: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, but is guilty of an eternal sin."
verses.3:30: For they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
verses.3:31: Then His mother and His brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to Him, calling for Him.
verses.3:32: And a multitude was sitting around Him, and they said to Him, "Behold, Your mother and Your brothers are outside seeking You."
verses.3:33: And He answered them, saying, "Who are My mother and My brothers?"
verses.3:34: And looking around at those who sat in a circle about Him, He said, "Behold My mother and My brothers!
verses.3:35: For whoever does the will of God, this one is My brother and sister and mother."
verses.4:1: And again He began to teach beside the sea. And a very great multitude gathered to Him, so that He stepped into a boat and sat upon the sea, and all the multitude was on the land beside the sea.
verses.4:2: And He taught them many things in parables, and spoke to them in His teaching:
verses.4:3: "Listen! Behold, the sower went forth to sow.
verses.4:4: And it came to pass, as he sowed, that some fell along the pathway, and the birds came and devoured it.
verses.4:5: And other seed fell upon rocky ground, where it did not have much soil; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
verses.4:6: And when the sun rose, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
verses.4:7: And other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
verses.4:8: And other seeds fell upon the good soil and yielded fruit, springing up and increasing, and brought forth thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
verses.4:9: And He said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.4:10: And when He was alone, those who were around Him, together with the twelve, asked Him concerning the parables.
verses.4:11: And He said to them, "To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given; but to those who are outside, all things come in parables,
verses.4:12: so that seeing they may see and yet not perceive, and hearing they may hear and yet not understand, lest they should turn back and it be forgiven them."
verses.4:13: And He said to them, "Do you not know this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?
verses.4:14: He who sows, sows the word.
verses.4:15: Now these are the ones along the pathway where the word is sown: when they have heard, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
verses.4:16: And these likewise are the ones sown upon rocky places, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy;
verses.4:17: and they have no root in themselves, but last only for a season; afterward, when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, immediately they stumble.
verses.4:18: And others are the ones sown among the thorns; these are they who have heard the word,
verses.4:19: and the cares of the age, and the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desires for other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.4:20: And those are the ones who were sown upon the good soil, such as hear the word and welcome it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
verses.4:21: And He said to them, "Is a lamp brought in to be placed beneath a grain measure or beneath a bed? Is it not to be set upon the lampstand?
verses.4:22: For nothing is hidden except that it may be made manifest, nor has anything been kept secret except that it should come into the open.
verses.4:23: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.4:24: And He said to them, "Take heed to what you hear. By the measure with which you measure, it shall be measured to you, and still more shall be added to you.
verses.4:25: For whoever has, to him it shall be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken away from him."
verses.4:26: And He said, "Thus is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed upon the earth,
verses.4:27: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should sprout and grow tall, though he himself does not know how.
verses.4:28: Of its own accord the earth brings forth fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain within the ear.
verses.4:29: And when the fruit is ripe, immediately he sends forth the sickle, because the harvest is at hand."
verses.4:30: And He said, "How shall we liken the kingdom of God, or with what parable shall we set it forth?
verses.4:31: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the earth, is smaller than all the seeds that are upon the earth—
verses.4:32: yet when it is sown, it rises up and becomes greater than all the garden herbs, and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of heaven are able to dwell beneath its shade."
verses.4:33: And by many such parables He spoke the word to them, according as they were able to hear.
verses.4:34: Yet without a parable He did not speak to them; and privately to His own disciples He explained all things.
verses.4:35: And He said to them on that day, when evening had come, "Let us pass over to the other side."
verses.4:36: And leaving the multitude, they took Him along, just as He was, in the boat; and other boats were with Him.
verses.4:37: And a great tempest of wind arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.
verses.4:38: And He Himself was in the stern, sleeping upon the cushion; and they awakened Him and said to Him, "Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?"
verses.4:39: And having awakened, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be silent! Be stilled!" And the wind subsided, and there came a great calm.
verses.4:40: And He said to them, "Why are you fearful? Do you still have no faith?"
verses.4:41: And they feared with a great fear, and said to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?"
verses.5:1: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.
verses.5:2: And as He came forth from the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met Him from the tombs,
verses.5:3: who had his dwelling place among the tombs; and no one was able to bind him any longer, not even with a chain,
verses.5:4: for he had many times been bound with fetters and chains, yet the chains had been torn apart by him and the fetters shattered in pieces; and no one had the strength to tame him.
verses.5:5: And continually, night and day, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and gashing himself with stones.
verses.5:6: And seeing Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down before Him,
verses.5:7: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What is there between me and You, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure You by God, do not torment me."
verses.5:8: For He was saying to him, "Come forth from the man, unclean spirit!"
verses.5:9: And He questioned him, "What is your name?" And he said to Him, "Legion is my name, for we are many."
verses.5:10: And he pleaded with Him earnestly that He would not send them out of the region.
verses.5:11: Now there was a great herd of swine feeding there beside the mountain.
verses.5:12: And they implored Him, saying, "Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them."
verses.5:13: And He permitted them. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the swine; and the herd rushed headlong down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand in number, and were drowned in the sea.
verses.5:14: And those who tended them fled and brought the report into the city and into the countryside; and they went out to see what it was that had come to pass.
verses.5:15: And they came to Jesus and beheld the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
verses.5:16: And those who had witnessed it related to them how it had come to pass with the demon-possessed man, and concerning the swine.
verses.5:17: And they began to implore Him to depart from their borders.
verses.5:18: And as He was entering the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed pleaded with Him that he might be with Him.
verses.5:19: And He did not permit him, but said to him, "Go to your house, to your own people, and report to them all that the Lord has done for you, and how He has had mercy upon you."
verses.5:20: And he went forth and began to proclaim in the Decapolis all the things Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.
verses.5:21: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a great multitude assembled around Him; and He was beside the sea.
verses.5:22: And there came one of the rulers of the synagogue, named Jairus; and seeing Him, he fell down at His feet
verses.5:23: and implored Him earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death; come and lay Your hands upon her, that she may be made well and live."
verses.5:24: And He went with him; and a great multitude followed Him and pressed hard upon Him.
verses.5:25: And a woman who had been afflicted with a flow of blood for twelve years,
verses.5:26: and had suffered many things under many physicians, and had spent all that she possessed, and had gained no benefit but had rather grown worse,
verses.5:27: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up from behind in the multitude and touched His garment.
verses.5:28: For she was saying, "If I may touch even His garments, I shall be made well."
verses.5:29: And immediately the fountain of her blood dried up, and she perceived in her body that she had been healed from the affliction.
verses.5:30: And immediately Jesus, recognizing within Himself that power had gone forth from Him, turned around in the multitude and said, "Who touched My garments?"
verses.5:31: And His disciples were saying to Him, "You see the multitude pressing hard upon You, and You say, 'Who touched Me?'"
verses.5:32: And He kept looking about to see the woman who had done this.
verses.5:33: Now the woman, afraid and trembling, aware of what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him and declared to Him all the truth.
verses.5:34: And He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you; depart in peace, and be whole from your affliction."
verses.5:35: While He was yet speaking, some came from the household of the ruler of the synagogue, saying, "Your daughter has died; why do you still trouble the Teacher?"
verses.5:36: But Jesus, disregarding the word being spoken, said to the ruler of the synagogue, "Do not fear; only believe."
verses.5:37: And He did not permit anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
verses.5:38: And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and He beheld a tumult, and those weeping and wailing greatly.
verses.5:39: And entering in, He said to them, "Why do you raise a tumult and weep? The child has not died, but is sleeping."
verses.5:40: And they laughed at Him in derision. Yet He put them all out, and took along the father of the child and the mother and those with Him, and entered where the child was.
verses.5:41: And taking hold of the child's hand, He said to her, "Talitha koum!" which is translated, "Little girl, to you I say, arise."
verses.5:42: And immediately the little girl rose up and walked about, for she was twelve years old; and immediately they were astounded with great astonishment.
verses.5:43: And He charged them strictly that no one should come to know this, and He directed that something be given to her to eat.
verses.6:1: And He departed from there and came into His native country, and His disciples followed Him.
verses.6:2: And when the Sabbath had come, He began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard Him were astonished, saying, "From where does this Man have these things? And what wisdom is this that has been given to Him, that such mighty works are performed through His hands?
verses.6:3: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are His sisters not here among us?" And they took offense at Him.
verses.6:4: And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor, except in his native country, among his own kinsmen, and in his own household."
verses.6:5: And He was unable to perform any mighty work there, except that He laid His hands upon a few who were sick and healed them.
verses.6:6: And He marveled on account of their unbelief. Then He went about through the surrounding villages, teaching.
verses.6:7: And He summoned the Twelve to Himself, and began to send them forth two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
verses.6:8: And He charged them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone—no bread, no traveler's bag, no copper money in their belt—
verses.6:9: but to be shod with sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
verses.6:10: And He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, abide there until you depart from that place.
verses.6:11: And if any place will not receive you, nor listen to you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust beneath your feet as a testimony against them."
verses.6:12: And going forth, they proclaimed that people should repent;
verses.6:13: and they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick, and healed them.
verses.6:14: And King Herod heard of it, for His name had become well known. And some were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead, and for this reason these powers are at work in Him."
verses.6:15: Others were saying, "He is Elijah." And others were saying, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."
verses.6:16: But when Herod heard of it, he said, "John, whom I beheaded—he has been raised!"
verses.6:17: For Herod himself had sent and seized John, and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
verses.6:18: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have the wife of your brother."
verses.6:19: Therefore Herodias held a grudge against him and desired to put him to death, yet she could not;
verses.6:20: for Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he listened to him gladly.
verses.6:21: Then an opportune day arrived when Herod, on his birthday, made a banquet for his nobles, his military commanders, and the foremost men of Galilee;
verses.6:22: and when his daughter Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those who reclined at table with him. And the king said to the girl, "Ask of me whatever you desire, and I will give it to you."
verses.6:23: And he swore to her, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give to you, up to half of my kingdom."
verses.6:24: And going out, she said to her mother, "What shall I ask?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptizer."
verses.6:25: And immediately she came in with haste to the king and made her request, saying, "I want you to give me at once, upon a platter, the head of John the Baptist."
verses.6:26: And the king was deeply grieved; yet because of his oaths and because of those who reclined with him, he was unwilling to refuse her.
verses.6:27: And immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded that his head be brought. So the executioner went and beheaded him in the prison,
verses.6:28: and brought his head upon a platter and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother.
verses.6:29: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his body and laid it in a tomb.
verses.6:30: And the apostles gathered together to Jesus and reported to Him everything that they had done and everything that they had taught.
verses.6:31: And He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a little while." For there were many coming and going, and they did not even have leisure to eat.
verses.6:32: So they departed in the boat to a desolate place by themselves.
verses.6:33: Yet many saw them departing and recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the cities and arrived before them.
verses.6:34: And when He went ashore, He saw a great multitude and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and He began to teach them many things.
verses.6:35: And when the day was already far spent, His disciples came to Him and said, "This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.
verses.6:36: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
verses.6:37: But He answered them, "You yourselves give them something to eat." And they said to Him, "Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"
verses.6:38: Then He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they had found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
verses.6:39: Then He commanded them to have all the people sit down in companies upon the green grass.
verses.6:40: So they sat down in orderly ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
verses.6:41: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people; and the two fish He divided among them all.
verses.6:42: And they all ate and were satisfied.
verses.6:43: And they took up twelve basketfuls of the broken pieces, and also of the fish.
verses.6:44: And those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
verses.6:45: And immediately He compelled His disciples to get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the multitude.
verses.6:46: And having taken leave of them, He departed to the mountain to pray.
verses.6:47: Now when evening had come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and He was alone upon the land.
verses.6:48: And seeing them hard-pressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night He came to them, walking upon the sea, and He intended to pass by them.
verses.6:49: But when they saw Him walking upon the sea, they supposed it was a phantom and cried out;
verses.6:50: for they all saw Him and were deeply troubled. Yet immediately He spoke with them and said to them, "Take courage! It is I; do not be afraid."
verses.6:51: And He went up into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. And they were utterly astonished within themselves,
verses.6:52: for they had not understood concerning the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
verses.6:53: And when they had crossed over to the land, they came to Gennesaret and moored at the shore.
verses.6:54: And as they came out of the boat, immediately the people recognized Him,
verses.6:55: and ran throughout that entire region, and began to carry about on pallets those who were ill, to wherever they heard that He was.
verses.6:56: And wherever He entered—into villages, or cities, or the countryside—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and implored Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched it were made well.
verses.7:1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, having come from Jerusalem, gathered together to Him,
verses.7:2: and seeing that certain of His disciples were eating their bread with defiled, that is, unwashed hands—
verses.7:3: for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands thoroughly, holding fast to the tradition of the elders;
verses.7:4: and coming from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves; and there are many other things which they have received to hold, such as the washings of cups, pitchers, and bronze vessels—
verses.7:5: then the Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with defiled hands?"
verses.7:6: And He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied rightly concerning you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors Me with their lips, yet their heart is far removed from Me;
verses.7:7: and in vain do they worship Me, teaching the ordinances of men as doctrines.'
verses.7:8: Forsaking the commandment of God, you hold fast to the tradition of men."
verses.7:9: And He said to them, "How finely you set aside the commandment of God, in order that you may keep your own tradition!
verses.7:10: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'He who reviles father or mother, let him surely die.'
verses.7:11: Yet you say, If a man says to his father or to his mother, 'Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban'—that is, a gift—
verses.7:12: you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or his mother,
verses.7:13: making void the word of God through your tradition which you have handed down; and you do many similar things like these."
verses.7:14: And having summoned the multitude again, He said to them, "Hear Me, all of you, and understand:
verses.7:15: there is nothing outside a man entering into him that can defile him; rather, the things which proceed out of a man are the things that defile a man."
verses.7:17: And when He had entered a house apart from the multitude, His disciples questioned Him about the parable.
verses.7:18: And He said to them, "Are you also thus without understanding? Do you not perceive that whatever enters into a man from outside cannot defile him,
verses.7:19: because it does not enter into his heart, but into his stomach, and passes out into the latrine?"—thus declaring all foods clean.
verses.7:20: And He went on to say, "That which proceeds out of a man, that is what defiles a man.
verses.7:21: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts: fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
verses.7:22: covetousness, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, arrogance, folly;
verses.7:23: all these evil things proceed from within and defile a man."
verses.7:24: And arising from there, He departed into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And having entered a house, He desired that no one should know it, yet He could not remain hidden;
verses.7:25: but immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, and coming, she fell down at His feet.
verses.7:26: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth; and she pleaded with Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.7:27: And He said to her, "Let the children be filled first; for it is not fitting to take the bread of the children and cast it to the little dogs."
verses.7:28: And she answered and said to Him, "Yes, Lord; yet even the little dogs under the table eat from the crumbs of the children."
verses.7:29: And He said to her, "Because of this saying, go; the demon has departed from your daughter."
verses.7:30: And when she went to her house, she found the child lying upon the bed, and the demon gone out.
verses.7:31: And again departing from the region of Tyre, He came by way of Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of Decapolis.
verses.7:32: And they brought to Him a man who was deaf and spoke with difficulty, and they pleaded with Him to lay His hand upon him.
verses.7:33: And taking him aside from the multitude privately, He put His fingers into his ears, and having spat, He touched his tongue;
verses.7:34: and looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, "Ephphatha," that is, "Be opened."
verses.7:35: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he began to speak clearly.
verses.7:36: And He charged them that they should tell no one; yet the more He charged them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
verses.7:37: And they were overwhelmingly astonished, saying, "He has done everything well: He causes both the deaf to hear and the mute to speak."
verses.8:1: In those days, when there was again a great multitude and they had nothing to eat, He called His disciples to Himself and said to them,
verses.8:2: "I am moved with compassion for the multitude, because they have now remained with Me three days and have nothing to eat;
verses.8:3: and if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will grow faint along the way; and some of them have come from afar."
verses.8:4: And His disciples answered Him, "Where will anyone be able to satisfy these people with bread here in a desolate place?"
verses.8:5: And He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They replied, "Seven."
verses.8:6: And He directed the multitude to recline upon the ground. Taking the seven loaves, He gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before them; and they set them before the multitude.
verses.8:7: And they had a few small fish; and after blessing them, He directed that these also be set before them.
verses.8:8: And they ate and were satisfied; and they gathered up seven large baskets of the broken pieces that remained.
verses.8:9: Now there were about four thousand people. And He sent them away.
verses.8:10: And immediately He entered the boat with His disciples and came into the district of Dalmanutha.
verses.8:11: And the Pharisees came forth and began to argue with Him, seeking from Him a sign out of heaven, testing Him.
verses.8:12: And sighing deeply within His spirit, He said, "Why does this generation seek a sign? Assuredly, I say to you, by no means shall a sign be given to this generation."
verses.8:13: And leaving them, He embarked again and departed to the other side.
verses.8:14: Now they had forgotten to take loaves, and except for one loaf they had none with them in the boat.
verses.8:15: And He solemnly charged them, saying, "Watch, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
verses.8:16: And they reasoned with one another because they had no bread.
verses.8:17: And knowing this, Jesus said to them, "Why are you reasoning because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Is your heart hardened?
verses.8:18: Though you have eyes, do you not see? And though you have ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
verses.8:19: when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you gather up?" They said to Him, "Twelve."
verses.8:20: "And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many large basketfuls of broken pieces did you gather up?" And they said, "Seven."
verses.8:21: And He said to them, "How is it that you do not yet understand?"
verses.8:22: And they came to Bethsaida; and some brought a blind man to Him and implored Him to touch him.
verses.8:23: And taking hold of the blind man's hand, He led him outside the village; and after spitting upon his eyes and laying His hands upon him, He asked him, "Do you see anything?"
verses.8:24: And looking up, he said, "I see men, for I perceive them like trees walking."
verses.8:25: Then He laid His hands upon his eyes again; and the man looked intently, was restored, and saw all things clearly.
verses.8:26: And He sent him away to his home, saying, "Do not even enter the village."
verses.8:27: And Jesus and His disciples went forth into the villages of Caesarea Philippi; and along the way He questioned His disciples, saying to them, "Who do men say that I am?"
verses.8:28: And they spoke to Him, saying, "John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets."
verses.8:29: And He asked them, "But you—who do you say that I am?" And Peter answered and said to Him, "You are the Christ."
verses.8:30: And He sternly warned them to tell no one concerning Him.
verses.8:31: And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be slain, and after three days rise again.
verses.8:32: And He was speaking this word plainly. And taking Him aside, Peter began to rebuke Him.
verses.8:33: But turning around and looking upon His disciples, He rebuked Peter and said, "Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not set your mind upon the things of God, but upon the things of men."
verses.8:34: And calling the multitude together with His disciples, He said to them, "If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
verses.8:35: For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; but whoever loses his life on account of Me and of the gospel shall save it.
verses.8:36: For what profit is it to a man to gain the entire world and suffer the loss of his soul?
verses.8:37: For what could a man give in exchange for his soul?
verses.8:38: For whoever is ashamed of Me and of My words amid this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man shall also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels."
verses.9:1: And He was saying to them, "Assuredly, I say to you that there are some of those standing here who shall by no means taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power."
verses.9:2: And after six days Jesus took with Him Peter and James and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves; and He was transfigured before them.
verses.9:3: And His garments became radiant, exceedingly white, such as no launderer on the earth can whiten so.
verses.9:4: And Elijah appeared to them together with Moses, and they were conversing with Jesus.
verses.9:5: And answering, Peter said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tabernacles—one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.9:6: For he did not know what to answer, because they had become terrified.
verses.9:7: And a cloud appeared, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is My beloved Son; listen to Him."
verses.9:8: And suddenly, having looked around, they saw no one anymore, except Jesus alone with them.
verses.9:9: And as they were descending from the mountain, He charged them that they should tell no one the things which they had seen, until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
verses.9:10: And they kept this saying close to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
verses.9:11: And they were questioning Him, saying, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must first come?"
verses.9:12: And He said to them, "Elijah indeed, coming first, restores all things. And how is it written concerning the Son of Man, that He should suffer many things and be held in contempt?
verses.9:13: But I say to you that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they desired, even as it is written concerning him."
verses.9:14: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a great multitude around them, and scribes disputing with them.
verses.9:15: And immediately the whole multitude, when they saw Him, were greatly astonished, and running up, they greeted Him.
verses.9:16: And He asked them, "What are you disputing among yourselves?"
verses.9:17: And one from the multitude answered Him, "Teacher, I have brought my son to You, who has a mute spirit;
verses.9:18: and wherever it seizes him, it dashes him down, and he foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth and becomes stiff. And I spoke to Your disciples that they might cast it out, and they were not able."
verses.9:19: And answering them, He said, "O unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I endure you? Bring him to Me."
verses.9:20: And they brought him to Him. And when the spirit saw Him, it immediately threw him into violent convulsions; and falling upon the ground, he rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
verses.9:21: And He asked his father, "How long a time has it been since this came upon him?" And he said, "From childhood;
verses.9:22: and many times it has cast him both into fire and into waters in order to destroy him. Yet if You are able to do anything, have compassion on us and help us."
verses.9:23: And Jesus said to him, "'If You are able'! All things are possible to the one who believes."
verses.9:24: At once, crying out, the father of the child said, "I believe; aid my unbelief!"
verses.9:25: And when Jesus saw that a multitude was running together, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him, and never enter into him again!"
verses.9:26: And crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out; and he became like one dead, so that most of them said that he had died.
verses.9:27: But Jesus, grasping his hand, raised him up, and he arose.
verses.9:28: And when He had entered a house, His disciples questioned Him privately, "Why were we unable to cast it out?"
verses.9:29: And He said to them, "This kind cannot come forth by anything except by prayer."
verses.9:30: And departing from there, they were passing through Galilee, and He did not wish for anyone to know.
verses.9:31: For He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is being delivered into the hands of men, and they will slay Him; and having been slain, after three days He shall rise."
verses.9:32: Yet they did not understand this saying, and they were afraid to question Him.
verses.9:33: And they came into Capernaum. And when He was in the house, He questioned them, "What were you debating along the way?"
verses.9:34: But they remained silent, for on the way they had disputed with one another as to who was the greatest.
verses.9:35: And sitting down, He summoned the twelve and said to them, "If anyone wishes to be first, he shall be the last of all and the servant of all."
verses.9:36: And taking a little child, He set him in their midst; and taking him in His arms, He said to them,
verses.9:37: "Whoever welcomes one of such little children in My name welcomes Me; and whoever welcomes Me does not welcome Me, but Him who sent Me."
verses.9:38: John said to Him, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we were forbidding him, because he was not following us."
verses.9:39: But Jesus said, "Do not forbid him, for there is no one who shall perform a mighty work in My name and soon be able to speak evil of Me;
verses.9:40: for anyone who is not against us is for us.
verses.9:41: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink on account of the name, because you belong to Christ, assuredly, I say to you that he shall by no means lose his reward.
verses.9:42: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him if a great millstone were fastened around his neck and he were cast into the sea.
verses.9:43: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than, having two hands, to depart into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
verses.9:45: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than, having two feet, to be cast into hell.
verses.9:47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be cast into hell,
verses.9:48: where their worm does not perish, and the fire is never quenched.
verses.9:49: For everyone shall be salted with fire.
verses.9:50: Salt is good; yet if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt within yourselves, and be at peace with one another."
verses.10:1: And arising from there, He came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan; and again multitudes gathered together to Him, and as was His custom, He taught them again.
verses.10:2: And Pharisees came forward and questioned Him whether it is lawful for a man to divorce a wife, testing Him.
verses.10:3: And He answered and said to them, "What did Moses command you?"
verses.10:4: And they said, "Moses permitted one to write a certificate of divorce and to put her away."
verses.10:5: And Jesus said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.
verses.10:6: Yet from the beginning of creation, He made them male and female.
verses.10:7: For this cause a man shall leave his father and his mother,
verses.10:8: and the two shall become one flesh; so then they are no longer two, but one flesh.
verses.10:9: Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no man separate."
verses.10:10: And in the house the disciples asked Him again concerning this matter.
verses.10:11: And He said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;
verses.10:12: and if she herself divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
verses.10:13: And they were bringing little children to Him so that He might touch them; yet the disciples rebuked them.
verses.10:14: When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, "Permit the little children to come to Me; do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
verses.10:15: Assuredly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child shall never enter into it."
verses.10:16: And taking them into His arms, He blessed them earnestly, laying His hands upon them.
verses.10:17: And as He was setting out on the road, a certain man ran up, knelt before Him, and asked Him, "Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?"
verses.10:18: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
verses.10:19: You know the commandments: 'Do not murder,' 'Do not commit adultery,' 'Do not steal,' 'Do not bear false witness,' 'Do not defraud,' 'Honor your father and mother.'"
verses.10:20: And he said to Him, "Teacher, all these things I have kept from my youth."
verses.10:21: And Jesus, looking upon him, loved him and said to him, "One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you possess and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.10:22: At this saying his countenance fell, and he went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.
verses.10:23: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, "How hard it shall be for those who possess wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!"
verses.10:24: And the disciples were amazed at His words. Yet Jesus answered again and said to them, "Children, how difficult it is to enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.10:25: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.10:26: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to Him, "Then who can be saved?"
verses.10:27: Looking upon them, Jesus said, "With men it is impossible, yet not with God; for all things are possible with God."
verses.10:28: Peter began to say to Him, "Behold, we have left all things and have followed You."
verses.10:29: Jesus said, "Assuredly, I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields, for My sake and for the sake of the gospel,
verses.10:30: who shall not receive a hundredfold now in this present time—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.
verses.10:31: Yet many who are first shall be last, and the last shall be first."
verses.10:32: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them; and they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. Then taking the twelve aside again, He began to tell them the things that were about to happen to Him:
verses.10:33: "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered over to the chief priests and to the scribes; and they shall condemn Him to death and deliver Him over to the Gentiles,
verses.10:34: and they shall mock Him, and spit upon Him, and scourge Him, and slay Him; and after three days He shall rise again."
verses.10:35: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Him, saying to Him, "Teacher, we desire that whatever we ask of You, You would do for us."
verses.10:36: And He said to them, "What do you desire that I should do for you?"
verses.10:37: And they said to Him, "Grant to us that we may sit, one at Your right hand and one at Your left, in Your glory."
verses.10:38: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
verses.10:39: And they said to Him, "We are able." And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you shall drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you shall be baptized;
verses.10:40: but to sit at My right hand or at My left is not Mine to grant, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
verses.10:41: And when the ten heard it, they began to be indignant concerning James and John.
verses.10:42: Then Jesus called them to Himself and said to them, "You know that those who are recognized as rulers over the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
verses.10:43: Yet it is not so among you; rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant,
verses.10:44: and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be bondservant of all.
verses.10:45: For indeed, the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many."
verses.10:46: And they came to Jericho. And as He was departing from Jericho with His disciples and a considerable multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
verses.10:47: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
verses.10:48: And many rebuked him that he should be silent; yet he cried out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.10:49: Then Jesus stood still and said, "Call him." So they called the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage! Rise up; He is calling you."
verses.10:50: And throwing aside his outer garment, he sprang up and came to Jesus.
verses.10:51: And Jesus answered and said to him, "What do you want Me to do for you?" And the blind man said to Him, "Rabboni, that I may recover my sight."
verses.10:52: Then Jesus said to him, "Go your way; your faith has made you well." And immediately he recovered his sight and followed Him along the road.
verses.11:1: And as they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, He sent forth two of His disciples,
verses.11:2: and said to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and immediately as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no man has yet sat. Untie it and bring it.
verses.11:3: And if anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord has need of it, and He will immediately send it back here.'"
verses.11:4: So they departed and found a colt tied by the door outside along the street, and they untied it.
verses.11:5: And some of those standing there said to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
verses.11:6: And they told them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.
verses.11:7: Then they brought the colt to Jesus and cast their garments upon it, and He sat upon it.
verses.11:8: And many spread their garments upon the road, and others spread leafy branches cut from the fields.
verses.11:9: And those who went ahead and those who followed cried out, "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!
verses.11:10: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.11:11: And He entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and having looked around at everything, since the hour was already late, He departed to Bethany with the twelve.
verses.11:12: And on the following day, as they departed from Bethany, He became hungry.
verses.11:13: And seeing from a distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see whether He might find anything on it; and coming to it, He found nothing except leaves, for it was not the season of figs.
verses.11:14: And answering, He said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!" And His disciples heard it.
verses.11:15: Then they came to Jerusalem. And having entered the temple, He began to cast out those who were selling and those who were buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves,
verses.11:16: and He would not permit anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
verses.11:17: And He taught and said to them, "Is it not written, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations'? Yet you have made it a den of robbers."
verses.11:18: And the chief priests and the scribes heard of it and sought how they might destroy Him; for they feared Him, since the whole multitude was astonished at His teaching.
verses.11:19: And when evening arrived, they went forth outside the city.
verses.11:20: And as they were passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
verses.11:21: And Peter, calling it to mind, said to Him, "Rabbi, behold, the fig tree which You cursed has withered!"
verses.11:22: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have faith in God.
verses.11:23: Assuredly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and be cast into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he speaks will come to pass, it shall be done for him.
verses.11:24: Therefore I say to you, everything that you pray and ask for, believe that you have received it, and it shall be yours.
verses.11:25: And whenever you stand praying, forgive if you hold anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses."
verses.11:27: And they came once more to Jerusalem. And while He was walking about in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to Him,
verses.11:28: and said to Him, "By what authority do You do these things? Or who gave You this authority, that You should do these things?"
verses.11:29: And Jesus said to them, "I too will ask you one question; answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things:
verses.11:30: Was John's baptism from heaven or from men? Answer Me."
verses.11:31: And they deliberated among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will reply, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
verses.11:32: But shall we say, 'From men'?"—they feared the multitude, for all held that John was truly a prophet.
verses.11:33: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know." And Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
verses.12:1: And He began speaking to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a winepress vat, and built a tower; and he leased it to vinedressers and went abroad.
verses.12:2: And at the proper season he sent a servant to the vinedressers, that he might receive from the vinedressers some of the fruits of the vineyard.
verses.12:3: And seizing him, they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.12:4: And again he sent another servant to them; and that one they wounded in the head and treated shamefully.
verses.12:5: And he sent another, and that one they slew; and many others, beating some and slaying others.
verses.12:6: He still had one, a beloved son; last of all he sent him to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.12:7: But those vinedressers said among themselves, 'This is the heir. Come, let us slay him, and the inheritance shall be ours.'
verses.12:8: And taking hold of him, they slew him and cast him out of the vineyard.
verses.12:9: What then will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the vinedressers, and give the vineyard to others.
verses.12:10: Have you not even read this Scripture: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner;
verses.12:11: from the Lord this came to pass, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
verses.12:12: And they sought to lay hold of Him, yet they feared the multitude, for they perceived that He spoke the parable against them. And leaving Him, they went away.
verses.12:13: And they sent to Him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they might ensnare Him in speech.
verses.12:14: And coming, they said to Him, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and defer to no one, for You do not look to the outward appearance of men, but in truth You teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not? Shall we pay, or shall we not pay?"
verses.12:15: But He, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, "Why do you test Me? Bring Me a denarius, that I may look at it."
verses.12:16: And they brought one. Then He said to them, "Whose image and inscription is this?" And they said to Him, "Caesar's."
verses.12:17: And Jesus said to them, "Render to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar, and to God the things that belong to God." And they marveled greatly at Him.
verses.12:18: Then Sadducees came to Him, who say that there is no resurrection; and they questioned Him, saying,
verses.12:19: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves behind a wife, and leaves no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.12:20: Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying, he left no offspring.
verses.12:21: And the second took her, and died without leaving offspring; and the third likewise.
verses.12:22: So the seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman also died.
verses.12:23: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife shall she be among them? For the seven had her as a wife."
verses.12:24: Jesus said to them, "Are you not in error for this very reason, because you do not know the Scriptures nor the power of God?
verses.12:25: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.
verses.12:26: But concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
verses.12:27: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly in error."
verses.12:28: Then one of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing together, and seeing that He had answered them well, he asked Him, "Which commandment is foremost of all?"
verses.12:29: Jesus answered, "The foremost is: 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one,
verses.12:30: and you shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.'
verses.12:31: The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."
verses.12:32: And the scribe said to Him, "Well said, Teacher; You have spoken in truth, that He is one, and there is no other besides Him;
verses.12:33: and to love Him with the whole heart, and with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is far more than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices."
verses.12:34: And when Jesus saw that he had answered with discernment, He said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And after that no one dared to question Him any longer.
verses.12:35: Then Jesus answered and said, as He taught in the temple, "How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?
verses.12:36: David himself declared in the Holy Spirit, 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand, until I place Your enemies beneath Your feet.'
verses.12:37: David himself calls Him Lord; how then is He his son?" And the great multitude heard Him gladly.
verses.12:38: And in His teaching He said, "Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk about in long robes, and to receive greetings in the marketplaces,
verses.12:39: and the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets;
verses.12:40: who devour the houses of widows, and for a pretense offer long prayers. These shall receive greater condemnation."
verses.12:41: And sitting down opposite the treasury, He watched how the multitude was casting money into the treasury; and many who were rich cast in much.
verses.12:42: And one poor widow came and cast in two lepta, which make a quadrans.
verses.12:43: Then He called His disciples to Himself and said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you that this poor widow has cast in more than all those who have been casting into the treasury;
verses.12:44: for they all cast in out of their abundance, whereas she, out of her poverty, cast in all that she possessed—her entire livelihood."
verses.13:1: And as He departed from the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, behold what manner of stones and what manner of buildings!"
verses.13:2: And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone shall be left here upon another that shall not be torn down."
verses.13:3: And as He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately:
verses.13:4: "Tell us, when shall these things take place, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?"
verses.13:5: Then Jesus began to say to them, "Take heed lest anyone lead you astray.
verses.13:6: Many shall come in My name, saying, 'I am He,' and shall lead many astray.
verses.13:7: And when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
verses.13:8: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there shall be earthquakes in various places; there shall be famines. These are the beginning of birth pangs.
verses.13:9: But keep watch over yourselves: they shall deliver you over to councils, and in synagogues you shall be beaten; and you shall stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.
verses.13:10: And to all the nations the gospel must first be proclaimed.
verses.13:11: And when they lead you away and deliver you over, do not be anxious beforehand concerning what you shall speak; rather, whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
verses.13:12: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and a father his child; and children shall rise up against parents and put them to death.
verses.13:13: And you shall be hated by all on account of My name; yet he who endures to the end, that one shall be saved.
verses.13:14: Now when you see the abomination of desolation standing where he ought not—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains;
verses.13:15: and let him who is upon the housetop not come down, nor enter to take anything out of his house;
verses.13:16: and let him who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
verses.13:17: Yet woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days!
verses.13:18: And pray that it may not come to pass in winter.
verses.13:19: For those days shall be such tribulation as has not occurred from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and shall by no means ever be.
verses.13:20: And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would be saved; yet for the sake of the elect, whom He chose, He cut short the days.
verses.13:21: And then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Christ!' or 'Behold, there He is!' do not believe it;
verses.13:22: for false christs and false prophets shall arise and display signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, the elect.
verses.13:23: But as for you, keep watch; behold, I have foretold all things to you.
verses.13:24: Yet in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give its radiance;
verses.13:25: and the stars shall be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens shall be shaken.
verses.13:26: And then they shall behold the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
verses.13:27: And then He shall send forth the angels and gather together His elect from the four winds, from the farthest end of the earth to the farthest end of heaven.
verses.13:28: Now from the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already grown tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near.
verses.13:29: Likewise you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that He is near, at the very doors.
verses.13:30: Assuredly, I say to you, this generation shall by no means pass away until all these things have come to pass.
verses.13:31: Heaven and earth shall pass away, yet My words shall never pass away.
verses.13:32: Now concerning that day or hour, no one knows—neither the angels in heaven nor the Son—except the Father.
verses.13:33: Take heed, keep alert, and pray, for you do not know when the time is.
verses.13:34: It is like a man journeying abroad, who left his house and gave his servants authority—to each one his work—and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
verses.13:35: Keep watch, therefore, for you do not know when the master of the house comes—whether at evening, or at midnight, or at the crowing of the rooster, or at dawn—
verses.13:36: lest, coming suddenly, he find you sleeping.
verses.13:37: And what I say to you, I say to all: Keep watch!"
verses.14:1: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize Him by deceit and put Him to death.
verses.14:2: For they were saying, "Not during the feast, lest there be a tumult of the people."
verses.14:3: And while He was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as He was reclining at table, a woman came having an alabaster flask of very precious ointment of genuine nard. And breaking the flask, she poured it upon His head.
verses.14:4: But there were some who felt indignation among themselves: "Why has this waste of the ointment taken place?
verses.14:5: For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor." And they were reproaching her sharply.
verses.14:6: But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why do you cause her trouble? She has performed a noble work for Me.
verses.14:7: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish, you are able to do good to them; but Me you do not always have.
verses.14:8: She has done what lay within her power; she anointed My body in advance for burial.
verses.14:9: And assuredly, I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what this woman has done shall also be spoken of in remembrance of her."
verses.14:10: Then Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests in order to betray Him to them.
verses.14:11: And when they heard it, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he kept seeking how he might betray Him at an opportune time.
verses.14:12: Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, His disciples said to Him, "Where do You wish us to go and make preparation, that You may eat the Passover?"
verses.14:13: And He sent two of His disciples and said to them, "Go into the city, and a man bearing a jar of water will meet you; follow him,
verses.14:14: and wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says: Where is My guest room in which I may eat the Passover with My disciples?'
verses.14:15: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready; and there make preparation for us."
verses.14:16: So the disciples went forth and entered the city, and found things just as He had told them; and they prepared the Passover.
verses.14:17: And when evening had come, He came with the twelve.
verses.14:18: And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "Assuredly, I say to you, one of you will betray Me—one who is eating with Me."
verses.14:19: They began to be sorrowful and to say to Him one by one, "Surely it is not I?"
verses.14:20: And He said to them, "It is one of the twelve, the one who is dipping with Me into the dish.
verses.14:21: For indeed the Son of Man goes just as it is written concerning Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.14:22: And while they were eating, He took bread, and having blessed it, He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take; this is My body."
verses.14:23: And taking a cup, and having given thanks, He gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
verses.14:24: And He said to them, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out on behalf of many.
verses.14:25: Assuredly, I say to you, I shall by no means drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
verses.14:26: And having sung a hymn, they went forth to the Mount of Olives.
verses.14:27: And Jesus said to them, "You shall all be made to stumble, for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.'
verses.14:28: Yet after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee."
verses.14:29: But Peter said to Him, "Even though all should be made to stumble, yet not I."
verses.14:30: And Jesus said to him, "Assuredly, I say to you, today—this very night—before a rooster crows twice, you yourself will deny Me three times."
verses.14:31: But he kept speaking all the more emphatically, "Even if I must die with You, I shall by no means deny You!" And in like manner they all kept saying the same.
verses.14:32: And they came to a place whose name was Gethsemane; and He said to His disciples, "Sit here while I pray."
verses.14:33: And He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and began to be filled with dread and deep anguish.
verses.14:34: And He said to them, "My soul is deeply sorrowful, even to death. Abide here and keep watch."
verses.14:35: And going forward a little way, He fell upon the ground and was praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from Him.
verses.14:36: And He said, "Abba, Father, all things are possible to You. Remove this cup from Me; yet not what I will, but what You will."
verses.14:37: Then He came and found them sleeping, and He said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not able to keep watch one hour?
verses.14:38: Keep watch and pray, lest you come into temptation. Indeed, the spirit is willing, yet the flesh is weak."
verses.14:39: And going away again, He prayed, speaking the same words.
verses.14:40: And returning again, He found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavily weighed down; and they did not know what to answer Him.
verses.14:41: Then He came the third time and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and taking your rest? It is enough! The hour has come; behold, the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
verses.14:42: Arise, let us be going! Behold, the one who betrays Me has drawn near."
verses.14:43: And immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a multitude with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
verses.14:44: Now the one betraying Him had given them an agreed signal, saying, "Whomever I kiss, He is the One; seize Him and lead Him away securely."
verses.14:45: And when he arrived, he immediately stepped up to Him and said, "Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
verses.14:46: Then they laid their hands on Him and seized Him.
verses.14:47: And a certain one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
verses.14:48: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs to arrest Me?
verses.14:49: Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me. Yet this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
verses.14:50: And forsaking Him, they all fled.
verses.14:51: Now a certain young man was following Him, wrapped in a linen cloth over his naked body; and they seized him,
verses.14:52: but leaving behind the linen cloth, he fled naked.
verses.14:53: And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes assembled together.
verses.14:54: And Peter followed Him from a distance, even inside into the courtyard of the high priest; and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself by the firelight.
verses.14:55: Now the chief priests and the entire council were seeking testimony against Jesus so as to put Him to death, yet they found none.
verses.14:56: For many were bearing false witness against Him, yet their testimonies did not agree.
verses.14:57: Then certain ones stood up and were bearing false witness against Him, saying,
verses.14:58: "We ourselves heard Him saying, 'I will tear down this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.'"
verses.14:59: Yet not even on this point did their testimony agree.
verses.14:60: And rising up in the midst, the high priest questioned Jesus, saying, "Do You make no answer? What is it that these men testify against You?"
verses.14:61: But He remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest questioned Him and said to Him, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
verses.14:62: And Jesus said, "I am; and you shall see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven."
verses.14:63: Then the high priest tore his garments and said, "What further need do we have of witnesses?
verses.14:64: You have heard the blasphemy! What is your judgment?" And they all condemned Him to be worthy of death.
verses.14:65: Then some began to spit upon Him, and to cover His face, and to strike Him with their fists, and to say to Him, "Prophesy!" And the officers received Him with blows.
verses.14:66: Now while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest came by,
verses.14:67: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him and said, "You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus."
verses.14:68: But he denied it, saying, "I do not know, nor do I understand what you are speaking of." And he went outside into the forecourt.
verses.14:69: And the servant girl saw him and began again to say to those standing by, "This man is one of them."
verses.14:70: But he denied it again. And after a little while, those who stood by again said to Peter, "Truly you are one of them, for indeed you are a Galilean."
verses.14:71: Then he began to invoke curses and to swear, "I do not know this man of whom you speak!"
verses.14:72: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times." And as he reflected upon it, he wept.
